_source: The Western Front Companion pp. 202-221 and Middlebrook appendices; mine count and Y Sap time from web sources (Wikipedia 'Mines on the first day of the Somme'). Times are 1 July 1916 unless stated.

mines.name: Hawthorn Ridge Redoubt
mines.effect: Blown ten minutes early; warned the Germans (RIR 119); crater 130 ft across and 58 ft deep; Germans occupied the rim

mines.name: Y Sap
mines.sector: III Corps, 34th Division, north of La Boisselle

mines.name: Lochnagar
mines.sector: III Corps, 34th Division, south of La Boisselle (Schwaben Höhe)

mines.name: Kasino Point
mines.effect: Fired after the infantry had left their trench; debris fell on the advancing men; destroyed the machine-gun post

minesTotal: 19 mines (8 large, 11 small) on the British front; the 11 small ones further south are not yet located

timeline.event: Final intense bombardment begins
Hawthorn Ridge mine; VIII Corps heavy artillery lifts off the German front line
Smoke screen laid; 56th Division leading companies move into no man's land
Stokes mortar hurricane bombardment
17th HLI creep forward towards the Leipzig Salient
109th Brigade (36th Division) leaves its trenches and creeps forward (15 min before the lift)
Smoke screen on the inner flanks of the two attacking divisions
Lochnagar, Y Sap and Tambour mines
Zero hour
1st South Staffords in Cemetery Trench, outskirts of Mametz
46th Division fourth wave goes over as the smoke clears; checked by machine guns
Schwaben Redoubt taken by 36th Division; 11th Border (32nd Division) caught moving up
90th Brigade (30th Division) begins the advance on Montauban
14th Brigade (1st Dorsets) advances on the Leipzig Redoubt
107th Brigade moves towards the German second line
29th Division attack has failed; 4th Division's 10th Brigade advance goes ahead though a halt order was sent
107th Brigade within 100 yards of the Grandcourt line and Stuff Redoubt, caught by its own barrage
30th Division's objectives including Montauban taken, about midday
50th Brigade (7th East Yorks, 7th Green Howards) attacks Fricourt after a weak bombardment; fails
7th Division's final effort; Mametz secured
18th Division reaches White Trench
21st Division ordered to consolidate
7th Division reaches Bunny Alley-Fritz Trench (map notes say about 19:00)
Heavier German counter-attacks force the 36th Division back from the Schwaben Redoubt
Only about 750 yards of the German front line still held by the 36th Division
Last company (1st Royal Irish Fusiliers) leaves the Quadrilateral
